edits.text: - Avoid cutting between a verb and its essential complement (object, resultative/degree complement, aspect particle): continuations commonly complete, reverse, or negate the predicate. A GOOD cut keeps the full verb phrase together; if unavoidable, cut after the complement or at a natural boundary that preserves predicate+core complement; score internal cuts low.

- When aspectual or clause-closing signals indicate an event is complete, cutting after them usually preserves event integrity. More generally, prefer cuts that keep a verb together with its essential complement (object, resultative, degree word, or aspect/particle). A GOOD cut ends after a complete predicate or lawful clause boundary; avoid cuts that leave a predicate awaiting completion, reversal, or negation.
